# tiny-input-sanitize

Zero-dependency input sanitization for 6 contexts: HTML, SQL literal, shell
argument, filename, log, and JSONPath. Single file.

## Run

```bash
pip install tiny-input-sanitize
```

## API

- `sanitize_text(value, *, context=None, allow=None, deny=None,
  max_length=None, strip_controls=True, normalize_unicode=True)`
  -> `SanitizationResult` — the general entry point.
- `sanitize_for_html(value, **kwargs)`
- `sanitize_for_sql_literal(value, **kwargs)`
- `sanitize_for_shell_arg(value, **kwargs)`
- `sanitize_for_filename(value, **kwargs)`
- `sanitize_for_log(value, **kwargs)`
- `sanitize_for_jsonpath(value, **kwargs)`
- `SanitizationContext` — enum of the 6 supported contexts.
- `SanitizationResult` — fields `value`, `context`, `applied_rules`,
  `original_length`, `confidence`; properties `is_clean` and
  `was_truncated`; method `to_dict()`.

## Usage

```python
from tiny_input_sanitize import sanitize_for_html

r = sanitize_for_html("<script>alert(1)</script>")
print(r.value)        # sanitized
print(r.confidence)   # 0.0-1.0
print(r.is_clean)     # False when a rule fired
```

## Notes

- The confidence score reflects how much of the input was altered, so a
  caller can decide whether to accept a heavily rewritten value.
- Rules are additive: `allow`, `deny`, `max_length`, `strip_controls`,
  `normalize_unicode`.
- Context-specific sanitizers are the intended API; the generic
  `sanitize_text` needs an explicit context.

## Links

- Source: https://github.com/hussain-alsaibai/tiny-input-sanitize
- Part of the OpenClaw zero-dependency tiny-* ecosystem.
